content.title: Eid al-Fitr 2026 Moon Sighting in UAE: Chaand Raat Date, Moon Rise Time, Crescent Moon Visibility, Prayer Timings & All You Need to Know
content.text: As Ramadan 2026 nears its final days, Muslims across the United Arab Emirates are eagerly waiting for the sighting of the Shawwal crescent moon — a moment that determines the end of fasting and the beginning of Eid al-Fitr. Astronomers and moon-sighting committees are observing the skies closely to assess visibility conditions, which this year are expected to be challenging. While scientific calculations predict a likely date, the final decision will come after official moon sighting reports from across the Emirates. Traditionally, the evening of Chaand Raat fills streets with last-minute shopping, festive atmosphere, and communal anticipation. UAE authorities and residents alike prepare for prayers, celebrations, and holidays as they await confirmation. Regardless of the sighting outcome, Eid in the UAE is a period marked by spiritual reflection, community gatherings, and joyous observance across all seven emirates. You Might Be Interested In Eid al-Fitr 2026 in the UAE Available astronomical projections and assessments from the Sharjah Academy for Astronomy, Space Sciences and Technology indicate that Eid al-Fitr 2026 is likely to fall on Friday, March 20, 2026, after Ramadan completes 30 days. If the Shawwal crescent is sighted on the evening of March 18 (the 29th of Ramadan), Eid would be celebrated on Thursday, March 19. However, the latest predictions show that the crescent will most likely not be visible on March 18 due to its position relative to the sun, making March 19 a more probable date for completing the holy month. Eid al-Fitr 2026 Moon Sighting Date in UAE (Chaand Raat Date) Chaand Raat in the UAE is expected on Wednesday evening, March 18, 2026, which corresponds to the 29th day of Ramadan. On this evening, moon‑sighting committees and observers across the Emirates — including Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and other emirates — will attempt to sight the Shawwal crescent shortly after sunset. If visibility conditions are not favourable, the moon sighting will be resumed on the next evening, March 19. Eid al-Fitr 2026 Moon Sighting Time in UAE (Chaand Raat Time) Moon sighting in the UAE is scheduled shortly after sunset on March 18, 2026. Sunset times across major cities like Dubai and Abu Dhabi are expected to be around 6:25 PM to 6:33 PM — providing only a short window after Maghrib prayer for observers to look toward the western horizon. According to astronomical calculations, the crescent will likely be too close to the sun and set too quickly on March 18, making naked‑eye observation difficult or impossible across much of the Emirates. Instead, visibility is expected to improve on March 19 after sunset, when the moon will be higher and more illuminated. Eid al-Fitr 2026: Crescent Moon Visibility in the UAE Experts from UAE observatories describe the moon‑visibility conditions for March 18, 2026, as very unfavourable. This year’s astronomical alignment means: The moon will be very low on the western horizon at sunset It will have minimal illumination, making the crescent faint The moon may set before or shortly after the sun, leaving a narrow viewing window For these reasons, many astronomers expect the crescent to remain unseen on March 18, resulting in Ramadan completing 30 days and Eid beginning on March 20. Eid al-Fitr 2026: Prayer Timings in UAE Across the UAE, Eid prayers are scheduled shortly after sunrise on the day of Eid. Based on recent official announcements: Sunrise (approx): Around 6:15 AM – 6:25 AM in major emirates Eid Prayer: Typically 15–25 minutes after sunrise According to official prayer schedules, in Dubai, the Eid prayer will likely begin around 6:18 AM to 6:20 AM and in Abu Dhabi, around 6:20 AM, with similar timings in other Emirates. Authorities have also announced that, due to current directives, Eid prayers in 2026 will be held inside authorised mosques instead of open grounds for safety reasons. Eid al-Fitr 2026 Namaz Timings in UAE Mosques All seven Emirates will observe coordinated Eid prayer timings, with worshippers advised to arrive early due to expected crowds. Sample estimated timings based on official bulletins and local practices are: Eid Prayer: approx 6:15–6:25 AM across Emirates Fajr Prayer: early morning before sunrise Local mosque authorities typically release detailed timetables closer to the date to help residents prepare.
